facts.text: Founded by English shipbuilder William Fell in 1726, Fells Point grew into Baltimore’s deep‑water port and shipbuilding hub.
The neighborhood’s name comes from the Fell family, whose wealth passed to William’s son Edward, who helped shape the area in the 1760s.
In 1763, Fells Point was officially established along the north shore of Baltimore Harbor, marking the start of a bustling waterfront community.
During the War of 1812, British forces targeted Baltimore because of its commercial importance, and Fells Point’s docks were a key strategic point.
The annual Fell’s Point Privateer Festival, held each April, celebrates the area’s maritime heritage and attracts visitors to historic waterfront streets.
The neighborhood once housed a diverse mix of immigrants—Irish, Germans, Jews, Poles, Ukrainians, Russians, Czechs, and Slovaks—who built homes and businesses along the harbor.
